h: Steam trains, shopping and Fenland fresh air
p: If you're heading to Peterborough for an inflatable session, it's worth thinking about the shape of your day. Bouncing is intense, so a lot of families like to go in the morning when everyone's fresh, then use the afternoon for something slower. Make sure everyone has a proper breakfast, but not too big, because flinging yourself down air-filled slides on a full stomach is never a great idea.

For little train fans, the Nene Valley Railway is a heritage line running steam and diesel trains along the river between Peterborough and Wansford. It has connections with Thomas the Tank Engine, and seasonal events are hugely popular with families, so check the timetable before you go. Peterborough Museum in a fine old building on Priestgate has local history, archaeology and the odd spooky tale, and is a nice indoor option.

If you'd rather shop and eat, Queensgate shopping centre sits right in the middle of the city next to the cathedral precincts. A little further afield, Burghley House near Stamford is a grand Elizabethan stately home with deer park and gardens, and it makes a lovely trip on its way north. Peterborough's mainline station has fast trains to London and the north, so it's surprisingly easy to visit by rail. Whatever you pick, a bit of Fenland fresh air after an hour of indoor bouncing works wonders, and everyone will sleep well that night. The city's Embankment by the Nene also hosts events through the year, so keep an eye out for anything on during your visit.
